newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau to combat gang violence with new law.
newsitem.headline: Macau to combat gang violence with new law.

text.p: Macau governor General Vasco Rocha Vieira said on Friday his government was determined to combat bloody triad gang wars and crime in the Portuguese-run territory.
Vieira also said a new anti-triad law, to take effect on Monday, will give police and law courts stronger power to counter gangland violence and criminal activities.
"Under the law, police will have broader powers of investigation, evidence gathering and the arrest of suspects," he said in a statement.

Vieira's warning comes after Portuguese-administered Macau, which will be returned to China in 1999, was rocked by triad violence. Triads are secret criminal societies that operate in Hong Kong, Macau and southern China.
This week saw a homemade bomb hurled at the Macau Government Palace, gunmen opening fire in the grounds of a hotel and two cars set ablaze.

Police have linked the incidents to clashes between triad gangsters over proceeds from illegal protection and loan-sharking rackets feeding off the enclave's legal casino business, Macau's biggest money-spinning industry.
Macau police said on Friday they had taken three men into custody for alleged involvement in recent violent crimes and the trio were likely to appear before a district court on Saturday.
China's chief representative in the enclave, Wang Qiren, said this week that the law and order situation was worrying and that police efforts to tackle the violence were inadequate.
